quizzes.title: Planet Parade
quizzes.description: A quick lap around the Sun and the eight planets that orbit it.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.note: Mercury zips around the Sun once every 88 Earth days.

questions.q: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
questions.note: More than 1,000 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.

questions.q: What do we call a rock from space that lands on Earth?
questions.note: While it is still burning up in the sky, it is called a meteor.

questions.q: Which planet is best known for its bright, wide rings?
questions.note: All four giant planets have rings, but Saturn's are by far the easiest to see.

questions.q: Which is the hottest planet in our solar system?
questions.note: Venus's thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, making it hotter than Mercury.

questions.q: How many planets are there in our solar system?
questions.note: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006, leaving eight.

questions.q: Pluto is officially classified as a planet.
questions.note: Since 2006 Pluto has been classed as a dwarf planet.

questions.q: Which planet spins on its side, tilted by almost 98 degrees?
questions.note: Scientists think a huge collision long ago knocked Uranus over.

questions.q: Which planet has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot?
questions.note: Astronomers have been watching this enormous storm since at least the 1800s.

questions.q: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
questions.note: Neptune takes about 165 Earth years to orbit the Sun once.

quizzes.title: One Small Step
quizzes.description: The launches, landings and pioneers of human spaceflight.

questions.q: Who became the first human in space in 1961?
questions.note: Gagarin orbited Earth once aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.

questions.q: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon during Apollo 11.
questions.note: Armstrong stepped out first, followed by Aldrin about 20 minutes later.

questions.q: In which year did Apollo 11 land on the Moon?
questions.note: The landing took place on 20 July 1969.

questions.q: Who became the first woman in space, in 1963?
questions.note: Accept "Tereshkova"; she flew solo aboard Vostok 6.

questions.q: What was the first artificial satellite, launched in 1957?
questions.note: Sputnik 1 was about the size of a beach ball and beeped radio signals back to Earth.

questions.q: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in the 1970s.
questions.note: Hubble was launched by the Space Shuttle in 1990.

questions.q: Which Apollo mission aborted its Moon landing after an oxygen tank exploded?
questions.note: The crew looped around the Moon and returned safely to Earth.

questions.q: Which dog became the first animal to orbit Earth, in 1957?
questions.note: Laika flew aboard Sputnik 2, just a month after Sputnik 1.

questions.q: Which Apollo 11 astronaut stayed in lunar orbit while the others walked on the Moon?
questions.note: Accept "Collins"; he piloted the command module Columbia.

questions.q: Which reusable NASA spacecraft carried crews into orbit from 1981 to 2011?
questions.note: The Shuttle fleet flew 135 missions in total.

quizzes.title: Starry, Starry Night
quizzes.description: From our own Sun to distant galaxies across the night sky.

questions.q: What type of star is our Sun?
questions.note: In about 5 billion years the Sun is expected to swell into a red giant.

questions.q: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our solar system?
questions.note: It is a spiral galaxy with hundreds of billions of stars.

questions.q: What is the nearest star to the Sun?
questions.note: Its light takes a little over four years to reach us.

questions.q: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
questions.note: So when you look at the Sun, you see it as it was about 8 minutes ago.

questions.q: Apart from the Sun, which is the brightest star in the night sky?
questions.note: Sirius is nicknamed the Dog Star and sits in the constellation Canis Major.

questions.q: Which spiral galaxy, about 2.5 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye?
questions.note: It is one of the most distant things you can see without a telescope.

questions.q: The Sun is made mostly of iron.
questions.note: The Sun is almost entirely hydrogen and helium.

questions.q: What is the huge explosion of a star at the end of its life called?
questions.note: A supernova can briefly outshine an entire galaxy.

questions.q: Polaris is better known by what two-word name?
questions.note: Accept "Pole Star"; it sits almost directly above Earth's North Pole.

questions.q: Which constellation contains the stars Betelgeuse and Rigel?
questions.note: Orion is named after a hunter from Greek mythology.

quizzes.title: Deep Space Challenge
quizzes.description: Moons, black holes and the astronomers who mapped the heavens.

questions.q: Which astronomer published a Sun-centred model of the solar system in 1543?
questions.note: His book was published in the year he died.

questions.q: A light-year is a unit of time.
questions.note: It is a distance: how far light travels in a year, about 9.5 trillion km.

questions.q: What is the giant Martian volcano, about 2.5 times the height of Everest?
questions.note: Its base is roughly 600 km across.

questions.q: Which astronomer, born in 1564, discovered Jupiter's four largest moons?
questions.note: Accept "Galileo Galilei"; he spotted the moons in 1610.

questions.q: What is the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing can escape?
questions.note: Not even light can escape once it crosses the event horizon.

questions.q: What is the largest moon in our solar system?
questions.note: Jupiter's moon Ganymede is even bigger than the planet Mercury.

questions.q: Venus spins in the opposite direction to most of the planets.
questions.note: On Venus the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.

questions.q: Which moon of Saturn has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane?
questions.note: The Huygens probe landed on Titan in 2005.

questions.q: Which spacecraft, launched in 1977, was the first to reach interstellar space?
questions.note: It crossed into interstellar space in 2012; its twin Voyager 2 followed in 2018.

questions.q: In which region beyond Neptune does the dwarf planet Pluto orbit?
questions.note: The Kuiper Belt is home to countless icy bodies left over from the solar system's birth.
